articles.title: South Korea pushes for football season to switch to winter after unbearable summer
articles.summary: Why fainting fans and perspiring players are a worry for the Asian league seeking to follow Japan and align with Europe. South Korean football is trying to find the goldilocks time to play the K-League. Winters have long been too cold and, increasingly, summers are too hot.
body: Last week a survey revealed that more than 70% of 29 respondent coaches in Asia’s oldest professional league support a shift from the traditional March to November schedule to one that matches the European format, which starts in late August and has a winter break.

It is an old debate that has intensified of late along with the summer temperatures. The city of Yangsan reached 42.5 Celsius on 2 August, the highest since records began, and Seoul recorded 17 consecutive tropical nights, so defined when the temperature does not fall below 25 degrees.

Fans fainted in stadiums and coaches bemoaned the quality of play. It looks like it is only going to get worse. A December 2025 report from the Korea meteorological administration (KMA) found that temperatures in the country had risen 0.9 degrees from 2020 to 2024, a worrying amount given that the increase over the previous 100 years had been 1.9.

South Korea’s Pro Footballers Association (KPFA) called for a change. “The K League must transition … to protect players from the worsening climate crisis and punishing summer heat,” it said in a statement. “And to maintain the league’s leadership within Asia and its global competitiveness.”

articles.title: Ludek Miklosko, former West Ham and QPR goalkeeper, dies aged 64
articles.summary: Miklosko played 373 times for West Ham from 1990. He won 42 international caps from 1982. The former West Ham and QPR goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko has died at the age of 64. Miklosko, who won caps for Czechoslovakia and the Czech Republic, had been living with cancer.
body: Miklosko joined West Ham from Baník Ostrava in 1990 for £300,000 after a trial and helped the club win promotion to the top division in his first season. He left in 1998 having made 373 appearances, joining QPR, initially on loan.

Miklosko ended his career at QPR in 2001 and returned to West Ham, where he worked as a goalkeeping coach until 2010. He later worked for a sports agency before taking roles at Baník Ostrava as a board member and sporting director.
West Ham said Miklosko would “forever hold a special place in the hearts of the West Ham family”. The club described him as a “beloved, inspirational goalkeeper and gentle giant of a man”.
Miklosko played 40 times for Czechoslovakia and twice for the Czech Republic in an international career that began in 1982. He said in 2024 that he was withdrawing from cancer treatment.

articles.title: Honda changes F1 design boss after slow start to return
articles.summary: Honda changes the leadership of its Formula 1 engine programme after the Japanese manufacturer's disappointing start to its return to the sport this season.
body: Honda, who won four world titles with Red Bull and Max Verstappen from 2021-24, joined forces with Aston Martin as their works engine partner for 2026.
But the pair are 10th of 11 teams in the constructors' championship and have a best result of ninth for Fernando Alonso in the Dutch Grand Prix.
On Monday, Honda announced a new head of its engine development programme.
Yoichiro Fukao, the former deputy leader of the project, will become Large Project Leader of the F1 project.

articles.title: The Josh Allen rollercoaster is up and running again for the new NFL season
articles.summary: The Bills quarterback produced his usual thrills: a galloping touchdown run, a near game-ending mistake and a brilliant throw. Buffalo fans better hold on. Having Josh Allen as your quarterback is a bit like owning a high-performance sports car with an odd mechanical flaw that can’t be repaired.
body: In Buffalo’s 36-31 Sunday win over the Houston Texans, Bills fans saw all sides of the Allenmobile. The quarterback completed 20 of 29 passes for 334 yards, two touchdowns, no interceptions, and a passer rating of 130.5. He also ran the ball six times for 23 yards and two more touchdowns, the first a typical romp through the opposing defense.

A two-play sequence perfectly summarized the Allen rollercoaster. There was his desperation heave into the end zone with 1:48 left in the game when the Bills were down 31-30. Texans cornerback Kamari Lassiter dropped what should have been an easy game-sealing interception, which gave Allen the second chance he needed to thread the needle on this amazing 34-yard touchdown pass to receiver Joshua Palmer.

articles.title: How youth helped Nordqvist answer critics and deliver Solheim Cup win
articles.summary: Captain Anna Nordqvist's faith in Europe's young rookies paid off as they delivered crucial points in regaining the Solheim Cup with victory over the United States, writes Iain Carter.
body: Anna Nordqvist spoke in the build-up to the Solheim Cup about the European team being in a period of transition as she chose a line-up with four debutants.
Any fears about fielding rookies for the most pressure packed event in the women's game were proven unfounded in her team's thrilling 15-13 victory at Bernardus Golf last weekend.
Nastasia Nadaud (21), Julia Lopez Ramirez (23), Mimi Rhodes (24) and, eventually, Lottie Woad all delivered crucial points and gave an encouraging glimpse into Europe's future.
Three of the quartet were captain's picks, with the 22-year-old Woad the only debut automatic qualifier for the team that avenged defeat in Virginia two years ago.

articles.title: How is NI squad shaping up for quadruple-header?
articles.summary: Northern Ireland will face four Nations League games in 11 days later this month with injuries, summer switches and individual form all making for an interesting selection when Michael O'Neill names his panel on Tuesday.
body: Before changes to the international calendar brought in for this season, Northern Ireland would previously have already played their first two fixtures by this stage of September.

Under the new fixture list, manager Michael O'Neill will name a squad on Tuesday for a four-game window, beginning with an away trip to Georgia on 25 September and concluding at home to the same opposition on 5 October. In between they face Hungary in Belfast and Ukraine in Slovakia.

While not quite unprecedented - NI faced four Nations League games in 11 days during the summer of 2022 - the condensed schedule will certainly be a challenge for Northern Ireland and other countries with smaller population bases.

Star player Conor Bradley has not featured for club or country since knee surgery in January and O'Neill told BBC Sport NI this month that he always suspected the injury "was going to take longer than maybe some people were thinking" before adding it would be a "bonus" to see him in a green jersey before March 2027.

articles.title: VOTE for the HSS North Jersey Football Team of the Week for Week 2
articles.summary: After another wild week of the high school football season, it's time to look back on the top team performances. Read about the teams that stood out last week and let us know which one should be the HSS North Jersey Team of the Week in the poll at the bottom of this page. Voting closes at 5 p.m.
body: The Bears (1-1) rallied for a 22-14 victory over Belleville, with Jeremy Duran leading the charge. He rushed for 254 yards and three TDs. Jordan Correa had 12 tackles and an interception, Jack Walsh had 10 tackles, and Eddie Then and Misael Garcia combined on a safety.

The Bulldogs (3-0) own the inside track on the NJIC Meadowlands title with a 41-28 win over New Milford. Ethan Diaz rushed for 220 yards and three TDs. Evan Croker threw for 131 yards, with TD passes to Steven Spadaro and William Jones, and he returned an interception for a score.

The Mustangs (1-1) snapped a 10-game losing streak with a 22-0 victory over Eastside that marked their first shutout since September of 2023. Jacob Marchan had six tackles and Jarrett Rodriguez had a tackle for a safety. Euriel Watt rushed for 132 yards and two TDs.

The Huskies’ (1-1) fourth-quarter, 2-point conversion run was the difference in a 22-21 victory over Mahwah. Myles Donald threw for 189 yards, with TD passes of 77 and 80 yards to Eric Orso. Donald also ran for 49 yards, one TD, and the decisive conversion.

articles.summary: Peter Lovenrkands believes there were shades of Barry Ferguson in Dan Neil's performance on Sunday as Rangers stormed into the Premier Sports Cup semi-finals at Celtic's expense.
body: That was the verdict of Ferguson's former team-mate at Ibrox, Peter Lovenkrands, who was blown away by the former Sunderland midfielder after he scored twice in the 3-0 win.
"Dan Neil ran the show from the start," Lovenkrands said on BBC Radio Scotland.
"On the ball he never lost a pass, simple things, he was doing everything right.
"I've not seen a performance like that since Barry Ferguson in the way he controlled the midfield."

articles.title: Runner alleges racial abuse during Great North Run
articles.summary: A runner in the Great North Run says she was racially abused by a section of spectators. In a video on Instagram, running coach Emma Kirk-Odunubi said the incident happened at about the nine-mile mark of the 13.1-mile route from Newcastle to South Shields on Sunday.
body: She said she noticed England flags while passing through a residential area before hearing people shout: "Protect our kids. Protect our England."
"And as I went past them next to the roundabout, they booed me," Kirk-Odunubi said.
"People always say don't let running get political. When I am being booed because of the colour of my skin... I've been running for 10 years and never have I come across that in my life - ever."
She said it was her "worst experience" during a race and that "hate has no place in running".

body: The striker's goal was initially disallowed for offside on the pitch before VAR overturned the decision.

articles.title: Joe Brady took his shirt off after first Bills win and gave away his game ball
articles.summary: Joe Brady became the fourth coach in Buffalo Bills history to win his debut as the team's head coach. Then he became the first to rip off his shirt in the locker room afterward.
body: Brady's first regular-season victory as an NFL head coach produced quite the celebration after the Bills beat the Houston Texans 36-31 Sunday at Reliant Stadium.
Josh Allen started it. The Bills quarterback stood in front of the team holding a game ball and put Brady's accomplishment into perspective.
"It takes a lifetime to become a head coach in the NFL," Allen said. "Game ball, Joe Brady, first one."
Allen handed Brady the football and wrapped him in a hug as the locker room erupted.

articles.title: 'Pietersen will add spark' as he begins England white-ball coaching role
articles.summary: Kevin Pietersen is “buzzing” to be back with the England set-up, having joined the white-ball coaching staff for the series against Sri Lanka, according to interim head coach Marcus Trescothick.
body: Pietersen will serve as a specialist mentor through to the 2027 Cricket World Cup in Africa next year. He will link up with the squad this week ahead of England's first T20I against Sri Lanka on Tuesday, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 6pm, with the first ball at 6.30pm.

Trescothick and Pietersen were Ashes-winning team-mates during England's famous 2005 triumph, giving the former first-hand experience of the qualities and talents the latter can bring to the current team.
"He is buzzing about putting back on the England shirt or tracksuit, buzzing for the opportunity and it's really exciting," the England batting coach said of Pietersen.

"Having his presence around, and the knowledge he has about batting - he saw batting in a different light to many people - if we can tap into that and get that into our white-ball cricket, It's only going to benefit the team."
